title: Polynomial-time conditional function
statement: Let $p$ be a Boolean predicate on binary strings, and let $f$ and $g$ be functions from binary strings to binary strings. Suppose that the one-bit function $x\mapsto[p(x)]$ and both $f$ and $g$ are polynomial-time computable. Then the function that returns $f(x)$ when $p(x)$ holds and $g(x)$ otherwise is polynomial-time computable.
hypotheses_covered: $p$ is a Boolean-valued function on binary strings
$f$ and $g$ are functions from binary strings to binary strings
The one-bit output function for $p$ is polynomial-time computable
replaced:
Let $p$ be a Boolean predicate on binary strings and $f, g$ functions on binary
strings. If the single-bit function $x \mapsto [p(x)]$ and both $f$ and $g$ are
polynomial-time computable, then so is the function mapping $x$ to $f(x)$ when
$p(x)$ holds and to $g(x)$ otherwise.
